items.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 42448389 'fix(security): close DNS guard gaps from CR (dns/promises, resolve*, proxy env)' (cm-main, May 2026), addressing a code-review finding on PR #476 marked CONFIRMED by a claim-verification subagent. ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit body, quoted): 'Strip proxy env vars in subprocess ... HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY ... would route fetch through an arbitrary target — DNS resolution happens at the proxy and the in-subprocess DNS guard never legitimately needs a proxy.' This is a deliberate SSRF-hardening fix, not an accidental regression — the bug report in #1039 asks to reverse it. REGRESSION_RISK: honouring HTTP_PROXY again without a proxy-aware SSRF check reopens the exact DNS-rebinding-via-proxy gap 42448389 closed as a confirmed security review finding. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any fix must add a resolved-target check for the proxy's own destination before honouring HTTP_PROXY, matching the dns.lookup/dnsPromises.lookup dual-patch pattern already in that commit; simply deleting the `delete process.env.HTTP_PROXY` lines is unsafe.
items.regressions: BLOCKER if the proxy env vars are restored without also adding the SSRF check 42448389's own commit message says is required; this is a real regression risk the map-I2 'B' bug classification understates — it is closer to a security decision than a plain bug.
items.related_closed_issues: PR #476 (the original SSRF hardening PR this traces to)
items.r3_wrong: no, r3 correctly kept it needs-decision; recommend elevating severity note
items.question: Does honouring HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY need a proxy-target SSRF check first (reusing 42448389's classifyIp pattern), or does v2 keep stripping and close #1039 as won't-fix?
items.recommendation: Classify as a security decision, not a plain bug-fix row; cite 42448389 explicitly in whichever ADR records the answer so a future contributor does not re-strip or re-honour the vars without reading the original CR thread.
